decisions.quote: Through replicating results previously found with this cohort at age 11-16 (Author 2 et al., 2015, Author 3 et al., 2016), we have shown that the average level of science capital among young people at age 17/18 has decreased, and that science capital is spread unevenly.
decisions.reason: The supplied accepted manuscript explicitly replicates the younger-cohort findings of 'Author 2 et al., 2015' (matching blind target 0 and the 2015 publication year of shipped row 5), but anonymizes self-citations in the text and reference list ('Author 2 et al. (2017; 2016; 2015; 2014; 2013)'), omitting the un-anonymized author names, title, and DOI (10.1002/tea.21227) needed to confirm or refute the full shipped citation from primary evidence alone.

decisions.quote: The present paper shows that science capital is patterned in inequitable ways, replicating previous results (from students aged 11-16) among students who are approaching the end of secondary school (aged 17/18).
decisions.reason: Although the shipped abstract quote is not in the supplied manuscript and the 2015 self-citation is anonymized as 'Author 2 et al., 2015' (blind target 0), both the overall conclusion and the specific discussion of Author 2 et al. (2015) (line 73) explicitly state that the age 17/18 results replicate the previous age 11-16 findings; age-related shifts in mean levels or effect magnitudes and new post-18 extensions do not alter the governing overall 'successful' replication verdict.
